_comment: Model date registry, the analogue of LiveCodeBench's lm_styles.py release_date field.
Every entry starts with "verified": false and the date check prints a warning when
it uses one. That is not modesty, it is the only defensible default: a benchmark
that filters on a training cutoff is only as trustworthy as the cutoff it was told,
and a number copied from memory into a config file is exactly how a contamination
claim quietly becomes false. Before citing a baseline, open the provider's model
card, paste the URL into "source", and flip "verified" to true.
declared_cutoff: the pretraining data cutoff the provider states.
release_date:    when the model became generally available. The default basis,
because the gap between cutoff and release is filled with
post-training data that is still data.
Either field may be null. A model with both null has no boundary, and every task
then classifies as UNDATED rather than SAFE.
